passages.note: House Final Reading roll call shows Gillette voting Y on HCR2060, which passed 31-29-0-0-0.
Bill status history confirms HCR2060's House Final vote on 06/04/2024 passed by the same 31-29-0-0-0 tally.

passages.provision_quote: the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin
passages.note: HCR2060's new illegal-entry article lets a court order a convicted recent border-crosser to return to a foreign nation, the state criminal-entry-law pattern the annex limits to recent crossers.

rows.reasoning: Gillette voted Y on HCR2060's House Final Reading (31-29-0-0-0); the bill's new illegal-entry article criminalizes entering Arizona outside a port of entry and lets a court order the convicted person to 'return to the foreign nation ... or the person's nation of origin.' This is a state criminal-entry law reaching only recent border-crossers, not 'all undocumented immigrants' or long-settled residents named in the rungs, so per the annex's hard case it shows only the enforcement direction, not a specific rung.
needs_source: Gillette's own statement (floor speech, press release, campaign material) tying his HCR2060 vote specifically to the illegal-entry/removal-order provision rather than the bill's benefits, fentanyl, or e-verify sections
